finding_verdicts.reason: The Markdown code span names the Datacircle MCP server. It does not contain a Ruby or shell command.
The backticks format MCP tool names. The workflow passes a catalog API name to a lookup tool, not to a shell.
The Markdown code spans label an MCP tool and its response fields. They do not invoke a shell or interpolate command input.
The URL is a reference to definitions for the catalog fields. The line does not instruct the agent to send data to that URL.
The URLs point to public catalog exports and a skill document. The line does not instruct the agent to download and execute content or upload data.

content.user_title: Compare Go-to-Market API Plans with Datacircle
content.value_statement: Go-to-market API pricing and limits are hard to compare across providers. Datacircle puts plan prices, scores, and technical details in one catalog and links to its sources.
actual_capabilities: List catalog APIs and show the number of plans and providers for each.
Look up plan rows for a named API.
Compare billing details, prices per 1,000 calls, and benchmark scores out of 100.
Compare reported rate limits, response speeds, and returned fields.
Include the source pages behind each shortlisted plan.
limitations: Tool-based lookups require a client connected to the Datacircle MCP server.
Results cover catalog entries and do not guarantee that every provider or plan is listed.
Catalog values can differ from current provider terms.
The skill does not call provider APIs or test their performance in your environment.

use_cases.title: Shortlist enrichment plans
use_cases.description: Find a few company enrichment plans and compare their reported unit prices before budgeting.

use_cases.title: Check integration requirements
use_cases.description: Compare returned fields, rate limits, and response speeds before choosing plans to test.

use_cases.title: Check vendor pricing sources
use_cases.description: Collect price and billing details with source pages for a purchasing review.

prompt_templates.title: Browse available APIs
prompt_templates.prompt: List the APIs in Datacircle. Show the number of providers and plans for each.

prompt_templates.title: Compare prices for one API
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the catalog API for [task]. Compare its top three plans by price per 1,000 calls, score, and billing terms. Cite the source pages.
prompt_templates.scenario: Build a short list for a known API task.

prompt_templates.title: Filter for integration needs
prompt_templates.prompt: Find plans for [API task] that return [required fields] and report at least [rate limit]. Mark missing values. Show price, score, speed, and source pages.

prompt_templates.title: Compare costs at expected volume
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare three plans for [API task] at [monthly call volume]. Cite sources and show unit price, score, billing limits, and required fields. Estimate monthly cost only if the listed terms support it.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a shortlist for a purchase decision.

output_examples.input: Show how a shortlist could compare two company enrichment plans.
output: Illustrative data only. These are not verified offers.
Example Plan A: $4 per 1,000 calls, with a score of 86 out of 100. Source type: provider pricing page.
Example Plan B: $3 per 1,000 calls, with a score of 78 out of 100. Source type: provider plan documentation.

output_examples.input: Show how to report an unlisted rate limit for a company lookup plan.
output: Illustrative data only. This is not a verified offer.
Example Plan C lists company domain and industry. It costs $6 per 1,000 calls and scores 82 out of 100.
Source type: provider plan page. The catalog does not report a rate limit, so the plan cannot be confirmed against your throughput requirement.

best_practices: State your call volume, required fields, and minimum rate limit before requesting a shortlist.
Compare a few plans and ask for the source pages behind each one.
Verify current prices, limits, and billing terms with the provider before choosing a plan.
anti_patterns: Treating a benchmark score as a guarantee of production performance.
Picking a plan from its unit price without checking billing terms or rate limits.
Passing credentials or customer records to a tool that only needs a public catalog API name.

faq.question: Do I need an API key?
faq.answer: The skill describes the Datacircle MCP server as public and does not require a key. Provider APIs may have separate access requirements.

faq.question: What do I need for tool-based lookups?
faq.answer: Connect the Datacircle MCP server to a client that can call its catalog tools.

faq.question: How are prices shown?
faq.answer: Catalog rows report a price per 1,000 calls alongside plan billing details.

faq.question: What does the score mean?
faq.answer: Datacircle reports its benchmark score on a 100-point scale. Use it alongside price, required fields, and technical limits.

faq.question: Can I view the catalog without MCP?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill links to public JSON and CSV exports that do not require sign-up.

faq.question: Are listed prices guaranteed to be current?
faq.answer: No. Check the cited provider pages for current prices and terms before making a purchase.
